variants.title: One tenant dominates a shard
variants.context: A single tenant creates 70% of all writes, but the data is stored in one shard.
variants.constraint: The hottest user still produces a hotspot.
variants.question: What is the correct fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Repartition by tenant or key so the hotspot is spread across several shards.

variants.title: Hot key in a hash range
variants.context: One user or key is accessed far more than others, causing one shard to saturate.
variants.constraint: The shard assignment is not balanced enough.
variants.question: What pattern addresses the bottleneck?
variants.expectedPattern: A better sharding strategy or key distribution that avoids hotspots.

variants.title: Large user table under heavy writes
variants.context: An application table keeps growing and a single database shard eventually shows 95% CPU.
variants.constraint: The data is still concentrated in one partition.
variants.question: How do you reduce the hotspot?
variants.expectedPattern: Shard the table based on a stable key or tenant distribution.
wrongChoices: Keep a single DB and increase memory
Route all traffic to a queue

variants.title: Cross-shard fan-out gets expensive
variants.context: The app starts sharding by user but some requests need data from many shards at once.
variants.constraint: A common query now touches multiple partitions.
variants.question: What is the tradeoff?
variants.expectedPattern: Revisit the access pattern and keep hot data local to avoid heavy cross-shard queries.

variants.title: New tenant creates skew after launch
variants.context: A new customer becomes very active overnight and one shard absorbs most traffic.
variants.constraint: Static shard layout is not resilient to skew.
variants.question: What should happen?
variants.expectedPattern: Rebalance or re-shard before the hotspot becomes permanent.
wrongChoices: Add a cache as the only defense

variants.title: Orders table struggles under broad writes
variants.context: Millions of orders are stored in one table and write traffic is spread more evenly than expected, yet one shard is still overloaded.
variants.constraint: The partitioning key is poorly chosen.
variants.question: What design mistake caused it?
variants.expectedPattern: The key choice creates uneven distribution and a hotspot despite multiple shards.

variants.title: Heavy read and write imbalance
variants.context: One shard gets all the writes and the others sit mostly idle.
variants.constraint: The app is horizontally scaled but the data model is still skewed.
variants.question: What does the system need to do?
variants.expectedPattern: Improve partitioning strategy so the read and write workload is spread more evenly.

variants.title: Queueing data on same shard
variants.context: Every new order is placed on the same partition because the sharding key is not random enough.
variants.constraint: Data is not evenly distributed across consumers.
variants.question: What should be changed?
variants.expectedPattern: Choose a better sharding key or a consistent hashing strategy that spreads the load.
wrongChoices: Move the queue before the database

variants.title: Shard growth after customer expansion
variants.context: One business customer expands quickly and all of its data starts landing in the same shard.
variants.constraint: A large tenant becomes the data hotspot.
variants.question: How do you keep the system healthy?
variants.expectedPattern: Split that tenant’s data across multiple shards or use a more granular key distribution.
wrongChoices: Keep all of one tenant in a single partition

variants.title: Geo-based partition seems simple but fails
variants.context: Data is partitioned by region, but one region’s traffic is far higher than the others.
variants.constraint: The partition map is static and some regions are much hotter than the rest.
variants.question: What is the design flaw?
variants.expectedPattern: Hot regions still need a balance strategy; geography alone does not prevent skew.
wrongChoices: Hot regions should never be used
